government.note: Unitary one-party socialist republic led by the Chinese Communist Party. Real power lies with the CCP General Secretary and the Politburo Standing Committee. Since 1993 the General Secretary has also been state President and Chairman of the Central Military Commission (the 'three-in-one' arrangement). The two-consecutive-term limit on the President and Vice President was removed by the 2018 constitutional amendment, so the President office carries no term_limit here. The Premier, appointed by the NPC on the President's nomination, is still limited to two consecutive five-year terms. The President can declare a state of emergency subject to NPC or NPC Standing Committee decisions.

system.note: Deputies are elected for five years by the people's congresses of the 22 provinces, 5 autonomous regions and 4 directly administered municipalities; the 9th NPC was the first with deputies for the Hong Kong SAR. The 9th NPC was elected October 1997 to February 1998 and sat 1998-2003, so seats_2000 is its composition. The NPC elects, and can remove, the President and other state officers by majority vote, but the CCP effectively makes the nominations and the Presidium has always put forward a single candidate, so the chamber is not treated as a confidence chamber.

chambers.review_note: The 9th NPC article gives 2,979 deputies and 2,130 CCP deputies, but a single figure of 460 for the eight other parties plus independents together, which leaves 389 deputies unaccounted for (2,130 + 460 = 2,590). Only the China Democratic League's own count (77) was found. The 772 'others' are every non-CCP deputy except the CDL: the other seven parties, non-party deputies and the unexplained remainder. The election results table in the list of presidents gives 2,983 total seats instead of 2,979. Check an official NPC source for the total and the per-party breakdown.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate only. China has no competitive national elections, so there is no vote share to derive from. The weights are a gameplay estimate: most support goes to the CCP's official line of a socialist market economy under one-party rule (market_socialist), with smaller shares for orthodox and Maoist currents, nationalist statism, liberal and social-democratic reform sentiment, and regional autonomy movements among Tibetans and Uyghurs. The eight United Front parties formally accept CCP leadership and are counted under market_socialist.

claims.note: The PRC regards Taiwan and its associated islands, governed by the Republic of China, as part of China and seeks unification. The Anti-Secession Law, ratified by the NPC on 14 March 2005, formalised (Article 8) the long-standing policy of using military means against Taiwan independence.
